text:
rachel: heads-up — while following the node quickstart I noticed logs showing the same X-Req-Id across multiple unrelated requests after a code reload (nodemon).

omar: interesting. dev hot reload can keep module-level singletons alive. which reqid lib are we using in the scaffold?

rachel: `redwood-reqid` from scaffold v2.0. it keeps a fallback id in module scope for some reason. sequence: start app → make a request → nodemon saves & restarts partial modules (HMR-ish) → subsequent requests in same process show duplicate reqid values for a bit.

claire: that smells like a cached fallback value that gets reattached to the logger context instead of being regenerated per-request. could also be OTEL context propagation reusing an old span as active context during hot reload.

omar: can you paste the snippet where reqid is generated?

rachel: sure snippet from scaffold:

```js
// reqid.js
let lastId = null;
module.exports = function getReqId(req) {
  if (req.headers['x-req-id']) return req.headers['x-req-id'];
  if (!lastId) lastId = `dev-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8)}`;
  return lastId;
}
```

rachel: ^^ right — that's the problem. lastId is preserved between reloads and reused until server fully restarts. it wasn't obvious at first.

patrick: oof. that pattern was put in place to make dev logs stable across restarts but it breaks uniqueness and can leak correlation between sessions. we should never fall back to a module-scoped id for requests.

claire: quick fix: make fallback id per-request and only stable for one request lifecycle, or prefer generating deterministic per-request ids from timestamp+counter, but never keep a cross-request cache. also ensure reqid middleware runs before any logging or otel autoinit.

omar: add a small guard: if process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' && hot-reload detected, still regenerate each request. but simpler: remove lastId entirely.

rachel: another wrinkle: when otel auto-inits (REDWOOD_OTEL=auto) it creates a global tracer that some devs reuse across reloads; combined with the cached lastId the logger bound to that tracer keeps the old id. so two things: remove module cache + make otel init per-request or rebind tracer after full restart.

patrick: recommended patches:
- update scaffold reqid to always return a fresh id if not provided in headers
- ensure reqid middleware is registered first in the middleware stack
- run redaction before logger snapshot and before any span attribute copy
- add a small integration test in quickstarts that simulates hot-reload + requests and asserts no reused reqid across requests

claire: for parity: python quickstart already generates fresh uuids per request and registers reqid first. Node scaffold diverged. we should sync templates and add a telemetry section in the quickstart README about hot-reload caveats.

rachel: I'll open a PR removing the module cache and add the test. will also include a note about REDWOOD_OTEL=auto behavior in dev.

hr-bot: created task RDW-telemetry-5318 assigned to rachel, omar. ETA: 3d. :spiral_calendar:

omar: thanks — small change but high impact. caught a tricky dev-only bug. :raised_hands:

claire: also update onboarding docs: "If you enable auto-OTEL in dev, expect ephemeral tracer state during hot reloads; prefer per-request tracer binding when iterating." short-term we should set REDWOOD_OTEL=0 in the Node quickstart by default.

rachel: PR draft: https://redwood-internal/pulls/5318-reqid-hotfix (includes unit + integration test). pushing now.

patrick: lovely. once merged let's run quickstart smoke on staging. thank you. :rocket:
